paper.title_en: Unpaired fractional excitations from many-body quantum geometry
paper.abstract_en: Compact scalar fields on lattices describe a broad class of many-body systems, from superconducting circuits to interacting bosons and spin systems. We show that a generic quantum geometric coupling between such fields induces a quantized Chern response, which in superconducting circuits can be interpreted as an integer-quantized gyration conductance. Because the fields are compact, these couplings produce Landau levels with finite degeneracy. Projected onto the lowest level, Josephson operators acting on different nodes acquire fractional exchange phases set by the Chern numbers. As a consequence, a junction shunting one node becomes periodic in a fraction of the flux quantum $h/2e$, and a gate charge on another node produces a charge counterpart of the fractional Josephson effect. In suitable networks, these operators encode Majorana fermions and their parafermion generalizations, each switched on by a single local Josephson junction, while the network itself supplies the nonlocal links that otherwise require long gate sequences. Single junctions then generate Hamiltonian terms containing unpaired encoded excitations, including parity-odd terms forbidden by Wigner superselection for elementary fermions, suggesting a route to all-to-all gates in fermionic quantum simulators.
